newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds seen climbing further on Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds seen climbing further on Greenspan.

text.p: Danish bond prices opened markedly higher on Wednesday, cheered by U.S. Fed Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's upbeat speech and dealers predicted more gains ahead in a strong market.
"Foreign investor interest in Danish bonds is solid. Greenspan's positive Humphrey Hawkins' comments have strengthened the market," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 opened up 0.36 point from Tuesday's close at 114.54, yielding 5.80 percent. The upcoming tone-setting seven percent 2007 bond was 0.40 point higher at 107.42, with yield at 6.00 percent.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 52. The crown opened at 3.8065 per mark, firming from Tuesday afternoon's 3.8070.
